# Story 01 — Web resource-file guard and matching-key check (Story: CRM-35)

## Prerequisites

- PLATFORM-10-WEB shipped `web/src/shared/i18n/` (`en.ts`, `ar.ts`, `index.tsx` with `I18nProvider`/`useTranslation`) and `web/src/shared/ui/primitives.test.tsx` already asserts the two key sets match — **do not rebuild any of that**.
- PLATFORM-9-WEB (the web-root scaffolding this story depends on per the intake) is on `main`; nothing in this plan changes routing, primitives, or provider wiring.
- CRM-26 web test harness (`web/src/testing/render.tsx` — `renderWithProviders(ui, { language: 'ar' })`) is in place and used by existing tests.
- Read `.squad/plan-lessons.md` first — in particular **L-13** (a source-scanning guard must read grammar, not prose) and **L-16** (prove the guard fails before believing it passes).

---

## Story Goal

Close the three real gaps left after PLATFORM-10-WEB so BR-6 ("two languages, always, in resource files, never hardcoded") is enforced, not merely observed:

1. Add a **narrow, grammar-aware** guard that fails the test suite when a page or feature source contains a user-facing string literal (JSX text nodes and the specific props that render user-visible text). Scope: `web/src/pages/**` and `web/src/features/**` only.
2. Close the one gap left by TypeScript's structural typing of `Messages`: a **key present in `ar.ts` but not in `en.ts`** (an extra Arabic key) currently passes `tsc`. Turn that into a build failure via the type system, so the second criterion ("build failure rather than a blank on a screen") is met at compile time and not just by a runtime test.
3. Prove strings are looked up **by key**: assert that no page code indexes the dictionary positionally (`Object.values(t)[n]`, `Object.keys(t)[n]`, numeric brackets on `t`).

Out of scope (and stated so a later story does not re-litigate): no i18next, no formatjs, no runtime language switching (LANGUAGES-2-WEB), no locale-aware date/number formatting (LANGUAGES-3-WEB), no cross-root missing-key check (LANGUAGES-4-ALL), no re-translation of the provisional Arabic text.

## Product rules (from story)

- **Current behaviour.** Both pages read every string through `useTranslation()`. `Messages` makes a **missing** key in `ar.ts` a compile error. A runtime test verifies key-set equality. Nothing stops the next page from typing a JSX literal, and an **extra** key in `ar.ts` compiles clean.
- **New behaviour.** A page or feature source that contains a user-facing string literal fails a test that names the file and the line. An extra key in `ar.ts` that `en.ts` does not have fails `tsc`. Positional dictionary access in page/feature code fails a test.

---

## Implementation tasks

No backend changes required. No new runtime dependency. All changes live under `web/`.

### 1 — Close the "extra key" gap in the resource-file types

**File: `web/src/shared/i18n/en.ts`** (edit lines 23–25).

The current `Messages` type widens values but does **not** constrain the section keys to those declared in `en`. TypeScript's structural subtyping means an object with an **additional** section on `ar` still satisfies `Messages`. Tighten the type so any section key on `ar` must also be a section key on `en`, and any leaf key inside a section must exist on the same `en` section. Keep values widened to `string` (the reason on lines 19–22 still holds).

Concretely, replace the `Messages` type with a shape that:
- Uses `keyof typeof en` as the exact section-key set (already true).
- Adds a companion type used by `ar.ts` that requires the **same section keys and the same leaf keys** — no more, no less — with `string` values. This is what closes the "extra key in `ar`" gap.

Suggested shape (executor may keep names but must match the intent):

```ts
// The dictionary the reader consumes: keys fixed by en, values widened to string.
export type Messages = {
  [Section in keyof typeof en]: { [Key in keyof (typeof en)[Section]]: string };
};

// The stricter shape ar.ts (and any future locale file) must satisfy: same keys,
// no extras. `Exact` uses an intersection with a "no other keys" clause so an
// additional section or an additional leaf key becomes a compile error.
export type LocaleOf<T> = {
  [Section in keyof T]: { [Key in keyof T[Section]]: string };
} & { [K in Exclude<PropertyKey, keyof T>]?: never };

export type Locale = LocaleOf<typeof en> & {
  [Section in keyof typeof en]: LocaleOf<(typeof en)[Section]>[Section] &
    { [K in Exclude<PropertyKey, keyof (typeof en)[Section]>]?: never };
};
```

If a simpler formulation covers **both** the extra-section and extra-leaf-key case with the current TS 7 checker, prefer it. What must be true after the edit: adding `foo: 'bar'` at the top of `ar` **or** inside `ar.signIn` fails `pnpm --dir web typecheck`.

**File: `web/src/shared/i18n/ar.ts`** (edit line 1 and line 7).

Change the imported type and the annotation from `Messages` to `Locale` (or whatever the new stricter alias is named):

```ts
import type { Locale } from './en';
// …
export const ar: Locale = { … };
```

Leave the values unchanged.

Keep the comment on lines 3–6, but adjust the wording to reflect that **both** a missing key and an extra key are now compile errors.

### 2 — Add the literal guard as a Vitest test

**Create file: `web/src/pages/no-hardcoded-strings.test.ts`.**

Location rationale: colocated with the sources it guards; picked up automatically by `vitest run`; ignored by production builds.

What the test does:

- Walk `web/src/pages/**/*.{ts,tsx}` and `web/src/features/**/*.{ts,tsx}` (the latter directory may not yet exist — `fs.existsSync` it and skip when absent). **Exclude** anything ending in `.test.ts`, `.test.tsx`, `.spec.ts`, `.spec.tsx`, `.stories.tsx`.
- For each file, strip `/* … */` and `// …` comments the same way `primitives.test.tsx` line 48 does. Also strip TypeScript string-literal types (e.g. `type X = 'foo' | 'bar'`) is not required — the productions below already exclude non-JSX contexts.
- Parse the source and flag **only** these two productions as user-facing literals:
  1. **JSX text nodes**: text between an opening JSX tag and its close that is not whitespace, is not entirely `{…}` expression, and is not inside a `<script>` or `<style>` (none of those exist in pages today).
  2. **String literals passed to a JSX attribute whose name is in a small allow-list of text-carrying props**: `aria-label`, `aria-description`, `aria-placeholder`, `aria-roledescription`, `aria-valuetext`, `placeholder`, `title`, `alt`. When the attribute value is a JSX expression (`{…}`) it is fine; when it is a raw string literal (`title="Sign in"`) it is a violation.
- What the guard **must not** flag (state each explicitly in a comment at the top of the test, for L-13):
  - Import paths (`from '../../shared/ui'`).
  - `className` values.
  - Route strings (`navigate('/', …)`).
  - Test ids and non-text HTML attributes: `id`, `name`, `type`, `autoComplete`, `htmlFor`, `role`, `data-*`, `key`, `href`, `src`, `rel`, `target`.
  - String-literal **types** (`type Language = 'en' | 'ar'`) and string-literal **union return values**.
  - Anything inside a `/* i18n-ignore */` block-comment (escape hatch for the rare case a future story finds; document it, but do not use it in current sources).

**Grammar, not prose (L-13).** Use a real parser, not regex over source text. Options in order of preference:
1. **TypeScript's own AST** via the `typescript` package — it is already a transitive dependency (via `typescript` itself, listed in `web/package.json` line 27). Use `ts.createSourceFile(file, code, ts.ScriptTarget.Latest, /*setParentNodes*/ true, ts.ScriptKind.TSX)` and visit `JsxText`, `JsxAttribute` and `StringLiteral` nodes. This adds no npm dependency.
2. If, when the executor tries option 1, the installed `typescript` version does not export the visitor helpers needed, fall back to `@babel/parser` + `@babel/traverse` — but only if step 1 is genuinely unworkable. Prefer option 1.

Report format when the test fails: one line per violation, `path/to/file.tsx:LINE:COLUMN — <production>: <literal>`. Then `expect(violations).toEqual([])`.

**Prove it fails (L-16).** In the same test file, add a second test that constructs a tiny in-memory TSX string containing:
- a JSX text node (`<Heading level={1}>Sign in</Heading>`),
- an offending `title` attribute (`<button title="Go">…</button>`),
- a benign `type="submit"` and `className="x"` and `id="email"`.

Run the same walker against the in-memory source (pass a fake filename) and assert that exactly the two offending literals are flagged and the three benign strings are not. This is the "prove it fails" seat-belt required by L-16, and it keeps the walker's grammar under test forever.

### 3 — Add the "by key" assertion

**Add to `web/src/pages/no-hardcoded-strings.test.ts`** a third test that, for every file the walker considers (same glob, same exclusions), asserts none of these patterns appear (raw regex over the comment-stripped source is fine here — the shape is unambiguous):

- `Object.values(t)` or `Object.entries(t)` when the receiver is the translation object.
- `Object.keys(t)[` followed by anything.
- Numeric index into `t` itself: `t[0]`, `t[1]`, … (regex: `\bt\[\s*\d`).

Failure message: `<file>:<line> — dictionary accessed by index or position; use t.section.key`.

Leave `web/src/shared/ui/primitives.test.tsx` lines 65–76 alone. The runtime equality test is now a belt over the type suspenders; it stays because it also catches a hand-editing mistake in `ar.ts` that a broken build would otherwise mask.

## Edge Cases & Failure Modes

- **Empty page directory.** If `web/src/features/` does not exist, the walker returns `[]` for that root and the test still runs against `web/src/pages/`. Enforced by `fs.existsSync` before `readdirSync`.
- **Only-whitespace JSX text.** `<Card>   \n   <Heading …/></Card>` must not flag. Enforced by `text.trim() === ''` before treating a `JsxText` node as a literal.
- **JSX expression that happens to be a string literal.** `<Heading>{'Sign in'}</Heading>` — a `JsxExpression` wrapping a `StringLiteral`. The guard **must** flag it; otherwise the escape hatch is a one-character workaround. Enforced by inspecting `JsxExpression` children and matching a bare `StringLiteral`.
- **Unicode text.** Arabic literals (`title="مرحبا"`) must be flagged the same way as English ones. Enforced by matching on node kind, not on character range.
- **String-literal type on a page.** `type Variant = 'primary' | 'secondary'` in a page file must not flag. Enforced because such nodes are `LiteralType`/`TypeAliasDeclaration`, never `JsxText` or `JsxAttribute`.
- **JSX attribute expression.** `title={t.foo.bar}` must not flag: the attribute value is a `JsxExpression`, not a `StringLiteral`.
- **Numeric access to `t` inside a comment.** Comment stripping happens first; a comment containing `t[0]` is discarded before the "by key" scan.
- **Extra key in `ar.ts`.** After Task 1, adding `extraSection: { foo: 'x' }` at the top of `ar` must break `tsc`. Verified in Verification Step 3.
- **Missing key in `ar.ts`.** Already a compile error today via `Messages`; must remain so after the type change.
- **A future page under a nested directory.** The walker recurses; verified because it uses `readdirSync(..., { withFileTypes: true, recursive: true })` (or a manual recursion — recursive option is on Node 20+, which the api tests use; the web tests run under the same Node).
- **`Object.values(en)` outside a page file.** Only files under `pages/` and `features/` are scanned, so PLATFORM tests using `flatten(en)` are not affected.
- **Escape hatch abused.** `/* i18n-ignore */` is honored per-line; document that a plan review rejects a page that adds one without a rule-owner sign-off. No source uses it today.

## Migration / Rollback

Not a migration. If the guard is too aggressive in review, the shortest revert is:
1. Remove `web/src/pages/no-hardcoded-strings.test.ts`.
2. Revert the `Messages` → `Locale` rename in `web/src/shared/i18n/en.ts` and `web/src/shared/i18n/ar.ts`.

No data, no configuration, no on-disk state is touched. There is no partial-migration state to guard against.
